# Argus security audit — 2026-05-09

**Stack:** Python 3.12 + FastAPI + Google ADK + BigQuery Vector Search + Slack callback + A2A protocol
**Auditor stance:** hacker / pre-launch reviewer
**Methodology:** full read of every server, agent, tool, script, config, and test file under `projects/argus/`. Generated by the global `/security-audit` skill.

**26 findings: 4 CRITICAL, 7 HIGH, 9 MEDIUM, 6 LOW.** Fixed in PR (this branch); see SECURITY_MODEL.md for current enforcement table.

---

## CRITICAL

### C1 — Live Slack signing secret + bot token in plaintext on disk

**File:** `projects/argus/.env` (lines 9, 11)

`.env` is gitignored and not tracked, but exists on disk in plaintext containing real Slack secrets. Also contains a duplicate `SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET=` line (foot-gun for first-vs-last-wins dotenv parsers).

**Attack vector:** disk read, malware, accidental `git add -f`, sub-`.gitignore` override. With the signing secret an attacker forges any `/slack/interactions` POST.

**Impact:** Full takeover of approval channel.

**Fix in this PR:** code reads secrets via Secret Manager helper (env fallback for local dev only); secret-rotation runbook added; **operator must rotate at api.slack.com immediately — treat as already leaked.**

---

### C2 — `/a2a/argus/*` JSON-RPC endpoint has zero authentication

**File:** `projects/argus/app/fast_api_app.py` (lines 60–88, 92–98)

`A2AFastAPIApplication.add_routes_to_app` mounts the RPC route with no `Depends(...)`, no Bearer check, no IP allowlist. `tests/integration/test_server_e2e.py:46–151` confirms — `requests.post(A2A_RPC_URL, ...)` succeeds with no auth header.

**Attack vectors:** unbounded LLM/BQ cost burn, prompt-injection driving destructive tools (with H3/H4), trivial DoS.

**Fix in this PR:** API key auth dependency on the route. Caller passes `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; key from Secret Manager; `secrets.compare_digest` validation; 401 on missing/wrong.

---

### C3 — `/feedback` endpoint unauthenticated; no length cap; no rate limit

**File:** `projects/argus/app/fast_api_app.py` (lines 101–112), `app/app_utils/typing.py` (line 28)

`Feedback.text: str | None = ""` — no `max_length`. `score: int | float` — no bounds, accepts NaN/Inf. Body shipped verbatim to Cloud Logging.

**Attack vectors:** unbounded GCP Logging spend, log-injection, fake feedback poisoning future tuning data.

**Fix in this PR:** same auth dep as C2; `Field(..., max_length=2000)` on text; bounded `score` with `allow_inf_nan=False`.

---

### C4 — SQL injection in BigQuery `VECTOR_SEARCH` (f-string interpolation of `top_k`, `PROJECT`, embedding values)

**File:** `projects/argus/app/tools/bq_vector_search.py` (lines 43–64); `scripts/setup_bigquery.py` (lines 186–231)

Every interpolated value (PROJECT, top_k, embedding floats) concatenated via f-string. No `QueryJobConfig(query_parameters=...)`. Latent — currently `top_k` is hardcoded `5`, `PROJECT` from env — but one refactor away from exploitable.

**Attack vectors:** `top_k` injection (if any future caller plumbs user input), embedding-list-typing escape (string in float list → injection), PROJECT env templating from CI.

**Fix in this PR:** parameterized queries via `QueryJobConfig`; assert types of every embedding element; pin/validate PROJECT/DATASET/TABLE at module load time.

---

## HIGH

### H1 — Slack approval replay (no nonce / no `(ts, sig)` seen-set; `record_decision` overwrites unconditionally)

**Files:** `app/slack_router.py:32–55`; `app/tools/slack_approval.py:14, 121–123`

A captured 5-minute-fresh signed body can be replayed. `record_decision` writes to a process-global dict with no lock; concurrent replays race. No `(ts, sig)` deduplication.

**Fix in this PR:** TTL'd `(ts, sig)` seen-set in `slack_router.py`; reject duplicates. Approval state machine in `app/tools/approval_store.py` with `threading.Lock`; `correction_id` transitions atomically `pending → consumed`.

---

### H2 — Slack handler doesn't validate `team` / `channel` / `user` IDs

**File:** `app/slack_router.py` (lines 32–55)

Anyone in any Slack workspace where the bot is installed can click and approve. Worse with C1: an attacker who learned the secret crafts perfectly-signed payloads from outside Slack.

**Fix in this PR:** allowlists for `payload["team"]["id"]`, `payload["channel"]["id"]`, `payload["user"]["id"]` from env (`SLACK_APPROVED_TEAM_IDS`, `SLACK_APPROVED_CHANNEL_IDS`, `SLACK_APPROVER_USER_IDS`).

---

### H3 — `catalog_writer` is a sibling tool of the orchestrator with no precondition; LLM is the security boundary

**Files:** `app/agents/argus_orchestrator.py:11–53`; `app/agents/catalog_writer_agent.py`; `app/tools/catalog_writer.py:37`

The orchestrator's instruction explicitly teaches the model to construct auto-approval JSONs and pass them to `catalog_writer`. `write_correction_audit` then reads `approval.get("decision")` from a string the LLM constructed. No cryptographic / state-store proof.

**Exploit chain:** prompt-injection in catalog content → orchestrator forges `{"decision":"approved"}` → `catalog_writer` releases → `feedback_agent` poisons RAG.

**Fix in this PR:** server-side `approval_store` keyed by `correction_id`. `catalog_writer.write_correction_audit` ignores LLM-supplied `approval_json` for the decision; looks up state from store. Hard fails with audit row if state ≠ `approved`. Same for `feedback_agent`.

---

### H4 — No `before_model_callback` / `before_tool_callback` on any agent

**Files:** all `app/agents/*.py`

Every `Agent(...)` constructed without input-guard callbacks. Item JSON ships verbatim to the model.

**Fix in this PR:** `before_model_callback` on orchestrator that strips/escapes injection patterns ("ignore previous", "act as", control phrases, JSON braces in unexpected fields). Best-effort heuristic, defence-in-depth.

---

### H5 — Persistent RAG poisoning via `feedback_upsert`

**File:** `app/tools/feedback_upsert.py:23–78`

`row` built directly from violation/decision JSON with no validation. Poisoned approved row → high-similarity match → next item silently auto-applies.

**Fix in this PR:** length caps (1024 chars per string field); reject control characters / shell-meta in `corrected_value`; `inserted_by` server-side; H3's approval-state check applies here too.

**Deferred to known-gap:** quorum requirement on AUTO tier (top-K matches all approved by N distinct humans). Single-match auto-tier remains until quorum is wired.

---

### H6 — No CORS / TrustedHost middleware

**File:** `app/fast_api_app.py:92–98`

Becomes CRITICAL the moment any session/cookie auth is added.

**Fix in this PR:** `CORSMiddleware(allow_origins=[<explicit hosts>])`, `TrustedHostMiddleware(allowed_hosts=[<env list>])`.

---

### H7 — `pending_decisions` is process-global in-memory dict

**File:** `app/tools/slack_approval.py:14`

Multi-pod Cloud Run silently breaks (worker that received Slack click ≠ worker polling). Race conditions on `if key in store: store.pop(key)`. Lost on restart. Memory leak (no eviction).

**Fix in this PR:** `threading.Lock` for in-process consistency. TTL eviction (entries >1h dropped).
**Deferred to known-gap:** Firestore migration for multi-pod correctness.

---

## Clean — implemented correctly

- Slack HMAC uses `hmac.compare_digest` (timing-safe)
- Slack timestamp staleness enforced (±300s)
- Body read raw before parsing, then verified (correct ordering)
- Compliance cap forces PROPOSE tier on `allergen_statement` even on high composite
- All-rejected matches → FLAG (fail-closed)
- `.env` is gitignored, not tracked
- Telemetry mode `NO_CONTENT` — no prompt/response logging
- Pydantic models on feedback endpoint (schema validation)
- No `eval`, `exec`, `pickle.loads`, `subprocess.shell=True`, `yaml.load`, `marshal` anywhere
- Service-role isolation via no client-side secrets
